posts.hook: Your ads aren't too expensive. Your close rate is.
lines: Your ads aren't too expensive. Your close rate is.
Say you spend fifteen hundred a month on ads.
That gets you ten estimates.
You close three. That's five hundred dollars per job.
Most guys fix that with more ad money.
Close five of the same ten, it drops to three hundred.
Same ads. Same leads. Two more jobs.
Real talk, this won't fix a bad price or a bad crew.
Most jobs are lost after the estimate.
Homeowners say no when they can't picture the result.
Our own remodeling company went from three in ten to five or six in ten.

posts.caption:
Your ads aren't too expensive. Your close rate is.
$1,500 in ads, 10 estimates, 3 jobs = $500 a job. Close 5 of the same 10 and it's $300.

posts.hook: Your bid gets decided when you're not in the room.
lines: Your bid gets decided when you're not in the room.
Say you walk a bathroom with the wife on Tuesday.
She loves your ideas. You send the quote that night.
Thursday, she shows it to her husband.
He never met you. He never heard the ideas.
All he sees is twenty-two thousand dollars.
So the answer is, let's get more quotes.
Real talk, some of those deals were never yours.
But a lot die because the idea stayed in your head.
Send something he can see. Their own bathroom, finished.
Our own remodeling company went from three in ten to five or six in ten.

posts.caption:
Your bid gets decided when you're not in the room.

posts.hook: Add up the hours your lost estimates cost you.
lines: Add up the hours your lost estimates cost you.
Say you do twelve estimates a month.
An hour driving. An hour in the home.
Another hour writing the quote at night.
That's three hours each. Thirty-six hours a month.
If you close four, eight of them went nowhere.
That's twenty-four hours. Three full workdays, gone.
Real talk, you'll never close all of them. Nobody does.
But even two more yeses changes that math.
People say yes faster when they can see the finished room.
Our own remodeling company went from three in ten to five or six in ten.

posts.caption:

posts.hook: Paying for renderings on jobs you never win?
lines: Paying for renderings on jobs you never win?
Say a designer charges you three hundred per rendering.
You do ten estimates a month. You render all ten.
That's three thousand dollars.
You close three. Seven renderings, paid for nothing.
That's twenty-one hundred a month, straight out of your margin.
Skip the renderings, and you look like every other bid.
Real talk, good design still matters.
The fix: show the idea before you pay for design.
Two phone photos of their room, turned into the finished version.
Our own remodeling company went from three in ten to five or six in ten.

posts.hook: "Just email me the quote" is a warning sign.
lines: "Just email me the quote" is a warning sign.
Say five homeowners tell you that this month.
You spend your evenings writing all five.
Two reply. Three go quiet.
You follow up once. Twice. Nothing.
They didn't hate your price. They had nothing to look at.
A quote is a list of words and a number.
Real talk, some people are just collecting bids.
But the serious ones needed to see it.
Show them their own room, finished, before you leave the house.
Our own remodeling company went from three in ten to five or six in ten.

posts.hook: Your portfolio is selling someone else's kitchen.
lines: Your portfolio is selling someone else's kitchen.
Say you show a homeowner twenty photos of past jobs.
Beautiful work. Different house. Different layout.
They nod. Then they ask, but what would mine look like?
You say, trust me, it'll look great.
The next contractor says the same thing. For six grand less.
Now it comes down to price.
Real talk, your portfolio still builds trust. Keep it.
But trust doesn't close the job. Picturing their own room does.
Show them their kitchen, finished, from their own photos.
Our own remodeling company went from three in ten to five or six in ten.

posts.hook: Following up a week later? It's already gone.
lines: Following up a week later? It's already gone.
Say a homeowner gets three bids for a bathroom.
Yours lands Monday. The other two by Friday.
Over the weekend, they pick one.
You call the next Tuesday. They went with someone else.
Not the cheapest one. The one they could picture.
The decision happened while you were waiting.
Real talk, a faster follow-up won't save a weak bid.
In those first days, they need something to look at.
Their own bathroom, finished, on their phone the same night.
Our own remodeling company went from three in ten to five or six in ten.
